summary: The canonical G4 visual-language comparison requires the hash-pinned accepted pilot to be captured as the reference target using the same exhaustive actionful screen contract as the implementation target, but the accepted pilot cannot satisfy that target-screen interaction and environment contract without changing its bytes or injecting unpinned runtime behavior.
observations: screen_contract_ready requires interaction_contract.visible_actions to exact-cover every functional action, including UI-AUTH-001.inspect
capture_geometry.cjs executes interaction_contract.visible_actions for both reference and implementation targets
capture_geometry.cjs verifies fixture, font-bundle, and asset-bundle meta values for both reference and implementation targets
the accepted pilot contains neither data-prototype-action=UI-AUTH-001.inspect nor ui-fixture-sha256, ui-font-bundle-sha256, or ui-asset-bundle-sha256 meta bindings
visual_language_conformance requires the reference render-provenance source artifact to equal the accepted visual-authority path and SHA-256
a wrapper, injected subresource, edited pilot, or hand-authored receipt would invalidate provenance or violate the no-fake-fidelity and no-accepted-artifact-mutation rules
repair_boundary: A revisioned canonical capture/visual-QA contract must separate accepted visual-language reference capture from target-screen functional-action and fixture-meta execution, while retaining hash-pinned provenance and implementation-side interaction proof. This requires authority to change and release the installed ui-design-program skill contract; it is outside this stage's program-owned write scope.
forbidden_workarounds: inject unpinned script or markup into the reference render
point reference provenance at a candidate-derived artifact
hand-edit a passing capture, provenance, raster, visual-QA, screen-acceptance, family-acceptance, or transition receipt
